system_description.narrative_title: Fractured Alliances, Rising Regional Wars, and a Bond-Market Shock
system_description.narrative_summary: The global geopolitical order is an open, interacting system driven by major-power competition, multiple active conflict theatres (Ukraine, the Middle East, the Korean peninsula) and tightly coupled global markets and supply chains. A sharp sovereign bond selloff and unprecedented US Treasury buybacks have injected fiscal-monetary friction and market volatility that amplify geopolitical stress. Localised military strikes, diplomatic hedging and economic coercion (sanctions, tariffs, trade measures) are creating cascading risks across energy flows, trade routes and alliance networks.
system_description.scope: Inter-state geopolitics and security dynamics among major and regional powers (US, China, Russia, Iran, Israel, Turkey, North Korea, EU, Ukraine, etc.), allied and adversarial diplomatic and military interactions, global financial markets (sovereign debt and bond yields), and critical energy/commodity and trade channels that connect them.
system_description.super_system: The international political‑economic system — the global system of states, markets, institutions and transnational flows embedded within Planetary (environmental and resource) constraints.
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets & sovereign debt dynamics (Treasury market, bond yields, investor risk premia)
Energy and commodity supply chains (oil, grain, tanker routes, Strait of Hormuz, Black Sea exports)
Regional security theatres (Eastern Europe/Ukraine, Middle East/Syria/Iran/Israel, East Asia/Korea/Taiwan)
International trade & institutions (tariffs, trade negotiations, sanctions, multilateral forums)

variables.name: US–Iran strategic confrontation
variables.description: The United States and Iran are locked in an escalating mix of economic warfare, sanctions and military pressure that is shifting Gulf export patterns, shipping routes and regional security calculations.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine high‑intensity war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, supported by Western arms and finance, remain in a grinding, high‑intensity conflict whose battlefield dynamics and seaborne export disruptions are reshaping European security and global commodity flows.

variables.name: US sovereign debt and bond‑market stress
variables.description: Soaring US federal borrowing, surging Treasury yields and aggressive Treasury buybacks are altering the global safe‑asset hierarchy, pressuring the dollar and constraining central bank policy options worldwide.

variables.name: Strain and realignment in US East Asia alliances
variables.description: US policy shifts and summit diplomacy with North Korea are prompting South Korea, Japan and other partners to recalibrate joint drills, deterrence postures and burden‑sharing, weakening longstanding alliance routines.

variables.name: Israel’s regional escalation and cross‑border strikes
variables.description: Israel’s campaign in Gaza and cross‑border strikes into Syria and Lebanon are intensifying frictions with Turkey and armed non‑state actors across the Levant, raising the risk of broader regional spillovers.
